title: Taranga 1. The Mangalacharana, Accounts of Various Matters, and a Brief Statement of the Birth of Srinivasa Acharya and Other Events
html:
Verses of blessing and the glorification of the Lord and His associates; Gopala Bhatta and his family; Narottama and Lokanatha; Shyamananda; the disciples of Srinivasa; why the book is called Bhakti-ratnakara; the ancestors of Jiva Gosvami, Rupa, Sanatana, Jiva and Raghunatha Dasa; the books of the Gosvamis; the birth of Srinivasa Acharya (in brief)

1O beautiful Gaurahari, abode of the auspiciousness of kirtana, ocean of great sweetness, ever bestowing the rasa of bhakti, shining golden mountain of prema, remover of all anarthas, You whose form is so dear, abode of pastimes and delights, sole Lord of the devotees of all the worlds — O Prabhu, be gracious!1

2O Sri Bhatta Gopala, bee at the lotus feet of the beautiful Gaura, sun dispelling the darkness of Mayavada, ocean of mercy, lord of the twice-born, O Prabhu! O son of the illustrious Venkata Bhatta, rich in the ornament of true and great bhakti, crusher of the disease of samsara, giver of joy to the hearts of the humble — protect me!

3O bee at the lotus feet of Sri Bhatta Gopala, uniquely skilled in giving away the jewel of bhakti, embodiment of love for the beautiful son of Shachi — protect me, O Prabhu Srinivasa, best of the twice-born!2

4I ever worship the branches of Prabhu Srinivasa, the wish-fulfilling tree of prema for Sri Krishna Chaitanya-chandra.

5The treasure of the Vaishnavas, remover of all anarthas — the book Bhakti-ratnakara: hear it, hear it with joy!

6Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the Lord of all,
who loves bhakti, whose form enchants the worlds,

7the Lord of Lakshmi, the son of Shachi and Jagannatha,
the treasure of the life of Nityananda, Advaita and Gadadhara!

8O Lord, the Vedas and the other scriptures sing Your glory;
who is not enchanted by these pastimes of Yours?

9Sri Guru, devotee, shakti, prakasha and avatara —
in all these forms, O Lord, is Your play.

10Thus the wise worship Your play —
and as instruction for others it is the cause of great good.

11Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-charitamrita: "I bow to the gurus, to the devotees of the Lord, to the avataras of the Lord, to His prakashas, to His shaktis, and to the Lord Himself, who is called Krishna Chaitanya."3

12Guru, Krishna, devotee, shakti, avatara and prakasha —
in these six forms Krishna performs His pastimes.

13Without mercy, who has the power to know this truth?
To others this play of Yours is inaccessible.

14You are Svayam Bhagavan, the shelter of all;
do what is fitting — I am afraid to ask for anything.

15Glory, glory to Sri Guru, the mine of the jewels of mercy,
the crest-jewel of those who give prema for Sri Krishna Chaitanya!

16Glory to Nityananda-Rama, the ocean of mercy,
the purifier of the worlds, the friend of the poor and suffering!

17You are the svarupa-prakasha of Prabhu Krishna Chaitanya;
You fulfil the desires of all [the devotees].

18Glory, glory to Sri Advaita-deva, the merciful,
who destroyed the terrible suffering of these souls!

19You are the avatara who is a part of Krishna Chaitanya;
who can describe Your glory, O Prabhu?

20Glory, glory to Gadadhara Pandita Gosani,
the foremost of the Lord's shaktis: there is no end to your virtues!

21Glory to Srivasa Pandita, the best of the Lord's devotees:
your life, rare even for the gods, is renowned!

22Glory to Sri Svarupa — fulfil my hope!
Glory to Vakreshvara, Sri Murari and Haridasa!

23Glory to Narahari, Gauridasa and Shuklambara!
Glory to Sri Mukunda, Vasu, Madhava and Shankara!4

24Glory to the great and noble Vidyanidhi Pundarika!
Glory to Vasudeva Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya!

25Glory to the illustrious Gadadhara Dasa Pandita!
Glory to Jagadisha, Kashishvara and Bhagavan!

26Glory, glory to Sri Paramananda Bhattacharya!
Glory to Krishnadasa Brahmachari, whose deeds are wondrous!

27Glory to the brahmana Haridasa and to the son of the Acharya!5
Glory to the lotus-eyed Raya Ramananda!

28Glory to Lokanatha and Sri Bhugarbha, full of prema!
Glory to Sanatana and Rupa, the abodes of rasa!

29Glory to Kashi Mishra, Gopikanta and Shashthidhara!
Glory to Abhirama, Vamshi, Saranga and Sundara!6

30Glory, glory to Sri Prabodhananda Sarasvati!
Glory to Sri Gopala Bhatta, the offspring of Venkata!

31Glory to Raghunatha Bhatta and Raghunatha Dasa!
Glory to Sri Raghava, who dwells in the forests of Govardhana!

32Glory to Sri Hridayananda, the jewel among acharyas!
Glory to Chiranjiva Sena and Sri Raghunandana!

33Glory to Kanu, Dhananjaya, Vijaya and Ramai!7
Glory to Sri Subuddhi Mishra and Sri Jiva Gosani!

34Glory to Bhagavatacharya, Madhava and Shridhara!
Glory to Vrindavana Dasa, the ocean of virtues!

35Glory to Krishnadasa Kaviraja Mahashaya!
Glory to Srinivasa Acharya, full of love for Gaura!

36Glory to Sri Thakura Mahashaya Narottama!
Glory to Shyamananda, the charming embodiment of bhakti!

37Glory, glory to all the devotees of Sri Chaitanya-chandra!
Who can tell how many they are — their names are the highest good.

38Countless are Chaitanya's devotees, boundless their deeds;
Sri Krishna Chaitanya is the one life of them all.

39The longing grows to tell the lives of the devotees,
full of prema-bhakti: the devotees' will is the [Lord's] delight.

40By the will of the devotees Gaurachandra descended,
and He plays wondrously with the devotees without cease.

41He whose end Brahma, Shiva and Shesha do not find —
such pastimes Gaura-raya performs in the age of Kali.

42Of three kinds are Chaitanya's pastimes, the abode of bliss;
their names are the Adi-khanda, the Madhya-khanda and the Shesha-khanda.8

43In the Adi-khanda it is chiefly the play of learning;
in the Madhya-khanda, Chaitanya's manifestation of kirtana;

44in the Shesha-khanda, His stay at Nilachala as a sannyasi,
having entrusted the land of Gauda to Nityananda.

45The crest-jewel of sannyasis, Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
together with Nityananda and Advaita blessed the age of Kali.

46Prabhu Sri Advaita and Nityananda-Haladhara
are bodies non-different from Sri Gaurachandra.

47Who can understand the doings of Nityananda and Advaita?
They always swim in the ocean of prema for Sri Chaitanya.

48Their nectarean talks with each other are like quarrels;
whose heart is not soothed on hearing them?

49Ah, ah, would that I could take all their troubles upon myself
and wander from land to land singing the virtues of them both!9

50Prabhu Gaurachandra, with Nityananda and Advaita,
plays in Sri Navadvipa in all kinds of ways.

51All these pastimes of the Lord are streams of nectar;
in great bliss the devotees drink them without end.

52The world becomes pure through Gauranga's pastimes;
one hostile to the Lord's devotees never gets a touch of them.

53He to whom the Lord's associates show favour
is the one who dives into the ocean of these pastimes.

54The pastimes are of two kinds, manifest and unmanifest:
now unmanifest play, now manifest play.

55As in the manifest, so in the unmanifest,
the Lord plays with His devotees without cease.

56The son of Shachi plays in Nadia for ever;
all the shastras clearly declare this.

57Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-bhagavata:
"Even today Gaura-raya performs those pastimes;
some fortunate souls are able to see them."10

58The Lord's abode, bhakti and associates are eternal;
whoever thinks otherwise about this is truly wretched.

59Thus [it is said]: "We eternally worship the one truth — Nityananda, Advaita and Chaitanya — eternally adorned with the brahma-sutra, shining in the eternal abode with eternal devotees and the eternal Bhakti-devi."11

60With all the devotees of all the avataras,
Vrindavana-chandra as Gaura plays in Nadia.

61Navadvipa and Vrindavana are one;
the Lord plays eternally in the forms of Gaura and Shyama.

62The wretch who sees a difference between Gaura and Krishna
sees a difference between Navadvipa and Vrindavana as well.

63For one whose life and treasure is Gaura-Krishna,
Navadvipa-Vrindavana is everything.

64The blissful play in Navadvipa and Vrindavana —
its essence is known to one on whom the devotees bestow their mercy.

65Would that I could take upon myself the troubles of such devotees of the Lord!
Now listen carefully to what I shall say.

66Earlier I composed a mangalacharana to Sri Bhatta;
in that same order I shall present my account.

67Sri Gopala Bhatta Prabhu is the root of the bliss of prema;
in every respect the treasure of his life is Gaurachandra.

68Srinivasa Acharya is the king of bhakti-rasa,
the recipient of Sri Bhatta's mercy, the embodiment of prema.

69The branches of Srinivasa Acharya Thakura
are all full of bhakti-rasa and known to the world.

70The nectar of their names I shall set out in full;
Gauranga with His associates is everything to them.

71Again and again I beg you: listen, friends —
make the feet of Krishna Chaitanya your all.

72One who is exclusively devoted to the Lord has the Lord in his control;
this good fame of the Lord has spread throughout the world.

73Sri Krishna Chaitanya Prabhu is the life of the devotees;
apart from the devotees the Lord's mind turns to nothing else.

74By the Lord's will devotees are born in various places,
and when the time comes the Lord meets with them.

75The play of the meeting of the Lord and His devotee
the best of the wise have described in various ways.

76In whatever way they described it, all of it is true;
whoever raises false arguments about it perishes.

77If you say, "In one account I see a different way,"
know that the agreement lies in the difference of kalpas.12

78The devotee's will is stronger than the Lord's will:
the Lord knows how to honour His devotee.

79One devotee comes and meets the Lord,
while to another the Lord Himself goes and meets him in his home.

80The Lord met Sri Gopala Bhatta in the South
and in great mercy revealed Himself to him.

81Here I shall tell briefly about the Bhattas:
Sri Gopala Bhatta is the son of Venkata.

82Sri Venkata Bhatta lived in the South,
a distinguished brahmana, learned in all the shastras.

83Trimalla, Venkata and Sri Prabodhananda —
the treasure of the lives of these three brothers is Gaurachandra.

84Formerly they were worshippers of Lakshmi-Narayana;
by the Lord's mercy they became intoxicated with the rasa of Radha and Krishna.

85During His tour of the South, Prabhu Gaura-raya
spent four months happily in the Bhatta's house.

86Chaitanya-chandra's beautiful tour of the South
is described in detail in the Chaitanya-charitamrita.

87Gopala Bhatta's name is not mentioned there;
about Venkata Bhatta's family it says this:

88Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-charitamrita:
"A Sri Vaishnava named Sri Venkata Bhatta
invited the Lord with respect.13

89He brought Him to his own house and washed His feet,
and that water he drank together with his whole family."

90Elsewhere it is stated that Gopala is Venkata's son;14
when he drank the water from the Lord's feet, prema arose in him.

91However hard he tries, he cannot keep still;
abundant pulaka sparkles on his body.

92How beautiful is Gopala, how lovely every limb!
His charming complexion surpasses the champaka.

93What a lotus of a face, what long eyes!
What brows, forehead and nose, what bright tilaka!

94What ears and cheeks, what a curve of the neck!
What arms, what a broad chest, what a slender waist!

95What knees and shanks, what exquisite feet!
His clothes and ornaments are incomparable.

96Moment by moment Gopala's beauty grows;
who, seeing the wondrous radiance, can stay composed?

97Having obtained the Lord of his life in his own home,
Sri Gopala, at his father's bidding, serves Him with great joy.

98Thus it is said by the ancients: "I praise Sri Bhatta Gopala, the best of brahmanas, the son of Venkata, appointed to the service of Sri Chaitanya Prabhu in his own home."15

99The mercy the Lord showed Sri Gopala Bhatta
I am unable to describe here in detail.

100Still, I shall tell a little of Gopala's life:
by his very nature he is ever devoted to the Lord's service.

101The Lord's sannyasa did not please Gopala;
going into solitude, he constantly lamented.

102To the Creator he speaks in a faltering voice:
"O Creator, why did you have me born in a distant land?

103You deprived me of the joy of the pastimes in Nadia
and showed me the Lord in this incongruous dress!

104The son of the king of Vraja, the Lord of Radhika's life —
you made Him accept sannyasa!"

105Saying this he drowns in the streams from both his eyes,
heaving long sighs like tongues of flame.

106And again he says: "Why be angry with the Creator?
I know it is only the fault of my own karma."

107Having said many such things he fell silent;
Gaurahari knew what was in Gopala's heart.

108Suddenly sleep overcame Gopala,
and in the guise of a dream Navadvipa appeared before his eyes.

109He sees there the wondrous play of the Lord
and plays together with the Lord — there is no limit to his happiness.

110Nityananda and Advaita, in the rapture of prema, embraced him;
and while they were saying who knows what, the sleep broke.

111Agitated, Gopala looks in every direction;
he walks before the Lord and cannot calm himself.

112Knowing that Gopala had come, [the Lord] rejoiced without bound
and became the beautiful dark one [Krishna] in the dress of a cowherd.

113Gopala in solitude contemplates this beauty —
and at that very moment [the Lord's] body became golden.16

114With the lustre of His form He enchants the worlds;
the knot of His curling hair falls down His back.

115On His forehead is sandal tilaka, His brows are Kamadeva's serpents;
the glance of His long eyes steals the chastity [of wives].

116He crushes the pride of hundreds of autumn moons;
in some new curve of His smile nectar pours down.

117He wears incomparable cloth tucked in the cowherd fashion;17
His body, adorned with jewels, stands in a captivating pose.

118A malati garland swings ceaselessly at His neck;
seeing this, Gopala was amazed at heart.

119He falls at His feet and again lifts his gaze to the Lord —
and at that moment he sees the crest-jewel of sannyasis.

120Prabhu Gaurachandra calmed Gopala
and gave him instruction which I cannot relate.

121And He said further: "Soon you will go to Vrindavana
and meet the rare jewels Rupa and Sanatana.

122The two of them will reveal what is in My heart,
and through your disciple it will spread throughout the world."18

123Saying this the Lord took Gopala on His lap
and drenched Gopala's body with the tears from His eyes.

124He said, "Keep all these words secret."
Supreme bliss filled Gopala's mind.

125Seeing Gopala's love for serving Gauranga,
Sri Venkata Bhatta was overjoyed.

126He gave Gopala over to the feet of Gaurachandra,
and he spends day and night in bliss with the Lord.

127"After four months the Lord will leave" —
at the very thought the three [brothers] lost their peace.

128Trimalla, Venkata and Sri Prabodhananda, all three,
reflect: "How shall we live without the Lord?

129Who will joke with us?
Who will take us with Him to bathe in the Kaveri?

130Who will sing sankirtana before Ranganatha?
Who will give us fallen ones that rare wealth of bhakti?

131For whose darshan will countless people come?
Without the Lord all these houses will be empty."

132So they speak, and tears flow from their eyes,
but they do not voice all the anxiety in their hearts.

133After four months the Lord took His leave;
the three brothers weep aloud.

134Sri Chaitanya departs from the Bhatta's house;
the Bhatta, rolling on the ground, falls at the Lord's feet.

135The Lord embraced the three brothers
and spoke many words of consolation.

136Having consoled Gopala, the Lord toured the South
and came to Nilachala to His devotees.

137Then came the journeys to Gauda and to Vrindavana and back,
and meetings with many devotees dear to Him.

138The crest-jewel of sannyasis, Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
blessed the souls of the age of Kali through His devotees.

139By the devotees' wish He lived in Nilachala;
what is in the Lord's heart He reveals to His devotees.

140Here, meanwhile, Sri Venkata Bhatta and his brothers, all three,
were deeply afflicted by separation from the Lord.

141How Gopala was without the Lord of his life —
who can describe it? Only one who saw it knows.

142At parting the Lord had embraced him
and commanded: "Soon your desire will be fulfilled."

143On those words he constantly reflects:
"After how many days will the Lord take me to Vrindavana?"

144Gopala is ever intoxicated with prema for Gauranga;
in expounding the truth of bhakti he is victorious everywhere.

145Everywhere he reveals the glory of Gaura's qualities
and refutes Mayavada without effort.

146Cultured people praise Gopala Bhatta:
"How did he acquire such learning?"

147Some say: "Sri Prabodhananda took care of him
and taught him from an early age.

148By his uncle's mercy he came to know all the shastras;
there is no one here as learned as Gopala."

149Others say: "Great are Prabodhananda's virtues;
his fame as Sarasvati has spread everywhere.

150Purna-brahman Sri Krishna Chaitanya Bhagavan —
apart from love for Him he knows nothing, even in dreams."

151[Thus it is said in] the Hari-bhakti-vilasa: "Gopala Bhatta, the disciple of Prabodhananda, who is dear to the Lord, gathers [the accounts of] the delights of bhakti, pleasing Raghunatha Dasa, Rupa and Sanatana."19

152Supreme renunciation, a charming embodiment of affection,
a great poet, incomparable in song, music and dance —

153such is Prabodhananda: hearing his verses everyone is filled with joy;
his greatness is boundless."

154So, with hearts full of great joy,
people speak of the virtues of Sri Prabodhananda and Gopala.

155Sri Gopala, the nephew of Prabodhananda,
is well brought up in every way and supremely kind;

156seeing him, his father and mother feel great happiness,
and he is always absorbed in the service of his parents.

157A venerable brahmana said to Venkata Bhatta:
"Your son is worthy in every respect.

158Such a way of bhakti we do not see here;
what wonderful love in his service to you both!"

159Hearing this, Venkata Bhatta with a joyful heart
tells of Gopala's conduct from his childhood:

160how he was at the darshan of Jagannatha in Nilachala,
how inspired he was in studying grammar and the other sciences,

161how he served the Purna-brahman Krishna Chaitanya —
all of it in order he told that brahmana.

162Having heard, the old brahmana, glad at heart,
praised Venkata and went home.

163Gopala's father and mother are greatly fortunate:
they gave their mind and life to the feet of Sri Chaitanya.

164Having allowed their son to go to Vrindavana,
both of them, remembering the Lord, left this world.

165After some time Gopala came to Vrindavana
and met Rupa and Sanatana.

166The all-knowing Lord in Nilachala at that very moment
knew that Gopala had come to Vrindavana.

167One day He set out joyfully from Mishra's house
to Gadadhara, [the servant] of Gopinatha.20

168The feelings Gorachand has for Gadadhara
are understood only as the fruit of great pious merit.

169What the relationship of Nityananda and Gadadhara is —
who has the power to tell even a particle of it?

170How Gadadhara deals with Advaita —
whose heart is not soothed on hearing of it?

171Srivasa Pandita loves Gadadhara Pandita
more than life and ever weeps over his virtues.

172The bliss Prabhu Haridasa feels
with Prabhu Gadadhara — who can express it?

173What wondrous love Gadadhara Pandita has
with Gadadhara Dasa — who can understand it?

174Sri Gaurasundara is Gadadhara's life;
[the Lord's] play with Gadadhara cannot be described.

175To the house of such a Gadadhara the Lord came
and sat down surrounded by the devotees.

176Who can describe that unprecedented beauty?
Fortunate people gaze from all sides.

177The crest-jewel of sannyasis, Prabhu Gaura-raya,
speaks to the devotees in sweet words:

178"For a long time I have had no news of Vraja,
and I do not know what is happening in My heart.

179I certainly want to send a letter there."
No sooner had He said this than a letter arrived from Vraja.

180In the letter Sri Rupa and Sanatana wrote
of Gopala Bhatta's arrival in Vrindavana.

181Hearing this, Mahaprabhu was very glad
and told everyone something about Gopala:

182"On My tour of the South, with great joy in My heart,
I stayed four months in the house of Venkata Bhatta.

183Gopala Bhatta is the son of Venkata Bhatta;
in a short time he became expert in all the shastras.

184Receiving his father's order, Gopala joyfully
served Me in countless special ways.

185Supremely merciful Krishna showed him mercy:
this is that Gopala Bhatta who has come to Vrindavana.

186Rupa and Sanatana are as dear to Me as life;
as soon as he arrived they wrote Me a letter."

187Hearing the Lord's very sweet words,
the devotees were filled with supreme bliss.

188Absorbed in the virtues of Rupa and Sanatana,
the Lord sends a letter to Vrindavana by [a messenger].21

189In the letter He writes to His dear Rupa and Sanatana:
"I am glad at Gopala's arrival.

190Regard Bhatta Gopala as your own brother,
and send good news from time to time.

191The books you have written and will yet write
will soon be spread everywhere.

192The one who will distribute the jewels of these books —
I think he has already appeared by Krishna's will."22

193With such a letter, giving [the messenger] clothes and other things,
He gladly sent him off in haste.

194He came to the Gosvamis in Vrindavana
and handed over the cord, the kaupina, the outer cloth and the letter.23

195The joy that came over everyone in Vrindavana
I cannot describe in detail.

196Sri Rupa and Sanatana, both full of prema,
have a wondrous affection for Sri Gopala Bhatta.

197In the Bhatta's mind arose the wish to compose a Vaishnava smriti;
Sanatana Gosvami knew of it at that very moment.

198And in Gopala's name Sri Sanatana Gosvami
composed the Sri Hari-bhakti-vilasa.24

199Gopala wished to serve a Deity —
and Sri Govinda gave a command to Sri Rupa in a dream.

200Sri Rupa Gosvami loves the Bhatta as his own life;
he entrusted him with the service of Sri Radha-ramana.25

201These matters will be set out more fully later;
Gopala Bhatta's doings are truly wondrous.

202With Lokanatha, Bhugarbha, Kashishvara Pandita,
Sri Paramananda and the learned Krishnadasa —

203how lovingly he dealt with them all
cannot be described with one mouth.

204In Vrindavana, always with Sanatana and Rupa,
he delights in talk of Sri Krishna Chaitanya.

205His heart is full of love for Sanatana;
in his wondrous friendship with Sri Rupa he is happy without cease.

206The Bhatta's only life is Sri Radha-ramana;
he is ceaselessly absorbed in the rasa of service.

207By his virtues he fulfils all desires;
seeing him, everyone in Vrindavana rejoices.

208Thus it is said by the ancients: "I bow to Gopala Bhatta, whose heart is flooded with love for Sanatana, who is distinguished in all things by his friendship with Sri Rupa, whose only life is Radha-ramana, who grants their desires to those who worship."

209Of these events of Sri Gopala Bhatta's life
some tell a little, and others tell nothing at all.

210Whoever, not grasping the essence, raises false arguments about this,
in his heart the seed of offence sprouts.

211The great rasikas, the poets of former times,
though able to describe it, did not describe it:

212thinking to themselves, "It will be described later,"
they leave it for the delight of all [the poets to come].

213Thakura Vrindavana described the pastimes of the Lord,
but did not describe the tour of the South and other things.

214He is Vyasa himself; who can understand his intention?
He says thus: "Vedavyasa will describe it later."26

215Krishnadasa Kaviraja, humbly bowing to him,
described the tour of the South and the rest in detail.

216Here and there he left [things] to be described
for the sake of the poets who would write afterwards.

217So a worshipful guru, having happily eaten rice and other dishes,
leaves remnants on the plate for his disciple.

218Such is the custom of poets, but there is no end to the describing;
give up false arguments and relish it, fortunate ones!

219The lives of the Lord and of the Lord's devotees
the poets attentively describe in various ways.

220Knowing that the devotees' will is strong,
the poets write addressing the devotees of the Lord.

221Krishnadasa Kaviraja, greatly delighted,
wrote his book after receiving the command of many.

222Sri Gopala Bhatta gladly gave his permission,
but forbade him to describe in the book anything concerning himself.

223Why he forbade it — who can understand?
He always considered himself the lowest of the low.

224The Kaviraja could not transgress his order:
he writes only his name and makes nothing else known.

225Lokanatha Gosvami too gave such an order;
this I heard from the lips of old Vaishnavas.27

226Others described a little of it in his absence;
truly extraordinary are the virtues of this Bhatta.

227The Bhatta's play of learning in Vrindavana
I have not disclosed here because of the bulk of the book.

228He wrote a commentary on the Krishna-karnamrita,
hearing which the Vaishnavas feel supreme bliss.

229Sri Gopala Bhatta, noble on the path of pure bhakti,
moment by moment performs extraordinary deeds.

230After some time Srinivasa came to him there,
and the Bhatta mercifully fulfilled his hope.

231Having become his disciple, Srinivasa, by the Lord's command,
came to Gauda and revealed there the books of bhakti.

232Through Sri Rupa and others the Lord revealed the shastras,
and to Srinivasa He gave the power to spread these books.

233Sri Thakura Mahashaya, non-different from the Acharya,
proclaimed these two shaktis in a verse of his own.

234Thus [it is said] in a verse by Sri Thakura Mahashaya: "Through one shakti, headed by Sri Rupa, the Lord reveals these books; through another shakti, named Sri Srinivasa, He spreads them. When will He who mercifully manifested these two shaktis on earth — the ocean of mercy Sri Chaitanya — come before my eyes?"

235Srinivasa Acharya, the crest-jewel of the knowers of shastra,
by spreading the shastras of bhakti made the earth rich.

236By the Lord's will he accepted many disciples;
Ramachandra, Gokula and others are known to the world.

237Ramachandra and Sri Gokulananda are abodes of prema;
in passing I shall tell a little about them here.

238Ramachandra and Govinda are brothers;
their father is Chiranjiva, their maternal grandfather Damodara.

239Damodara Sena lived in Shrikhanda;
his name as a great poet is known to the world.

240Thus [it is said] in Sri Govinda Kaviraja's drama Sangita-madhava: "In Patala Vasuki is eloquent, in heaven Brihaspati is eloquent; in Gauda Govardhana is generous, in Khanda — Damodara the poet."28

241Damodara the poet was skilled in argument;
no one could get the better of him in any way.

242A digvijayi, easily defeated by him,
in his chagrin cursed him: "Be without a son!"

243Damodara appeased him in every way,
and he said: "You will have a daughter, blessed in the world.

244From her two jewel-like sons will be born;
by their power all that is inauspicious will be destroyed."

245To this worthy brahmana a daughter named Sunanda was born;29
day by day she grew, blessed with beauty and virtues.

246All the women of Khanda praise her;
when she reached the age for marriage, they sought a bridegroom.

247The greatly fortunate Damodara Kaviraja
gave his daughter in marriage to Chiranjiva Sena.

248Fear of the bulk of the book arises in my mind,
so I cannot describe the wedding festivities in detail.

249On the bank of the Bhagirathi is the village of Kumaranagara;
many Vaishnavas live there, a beautiful place.

250In that village was the home of Chiranjiva Sena;
after his marriage he settled in Khanda.

251What shall I say of the life of Chiranjiva Sena?
All the people of Khanda regard him as their very life.

252A wise associate of Sri Chaitanya Prabhu,
his heart is ever mad with sankirtana.

253Chiranjiva of Khanda is known everywhere:
he made the poor and lowly vessels of bhakti-rasa.

254In the Chaitanya-charitamrita, where [the devotees'] meeting with the Lord is told,
Chiranjiva Sena of Khanda is mentioned.

255Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-charitamrita:
"Mukunda Dasa, Narahari, Sri Raghunandana,
Chiranjiva of Khanda, and Sulochana."30

256Chiranjiva Sena, highly learned in every way,
lives in Khanda with his wife.

257His wife, devoted to her husband, is like Arundhati,
of the finest character and extraordinary conduct.

258As were the father and mother, so was the son Ramachandra;
by his birth Ramachandra brought great joy.

259From infancy his conduct was captivating;
men and women see in him their second life.

260His form is full of great splendour, in beauty he is Madana;
in a short time he acquired great learning.

261Seeing Ramachandra, wise people reflect:
"This is a portion of some god; it cannot be otherwise.

262By his own will he appeared in a family of vaidyas,
and because of his human form no one can recognize him."

263Many Vaishnavas feel:
"If this one becomes a Vaishnava, many will become Vaishnavas."

264So many people say many things;
Ramachandra Sena draws all hearts to himself.

265How Srinivasa Acharya made him his disciple
is a very long story; I cannot set it out here.

266He received the title "Kaviraja" in Vrindavana;
of this I shall tell here.

267Sri Paramananda Bhattacharya, a treasury of prema,
Sri Jiva Gosvami and other residents of Vrindavana —

268all, hearing from his lips the verses he had composed,
with great joy gave him the title "Kaviraja".31

269Ramachandra Kaviraja, full of all virtues,
is the one with whom Narottama Mahashaya is one in soul.

270Thus [it is said] in the drama Sangita-madhava: "On the bank of the celestial river, in the town of [...], from Sri Chiranjiva Sena — honouring brahmanas, devoted to Vishnu, well known [even] to the chief minister of the king of Gauda — and from Sri Sunanda was born the excellent Sri Ramachandra; he, the king of poets, became truly one with the illustrious [Narottama]."32

271What the relationship of Ramachandra and Narottama is
I shall relate further on; here I shall say a little.

272Body, mind, life and name — the two have but one;
so the name "Kaviraja-Narottama" spread.

273Everyone says "Narottama-Kaviraja",
as if two words — like Nara-Narayana.

274"Ramachandra-Narottama" is known to the world;
a double name arose to gladden everyone.

275Both are supremely expert in all the shastras;
without effort they crushed great unbelievers.

276Ever skilled in bestowing pure bhakti,
they are exclusive rasikas, wisest in all doctrines.

277Thus [it is said] in the same work: "We bow to these two, who became a pair through great mutual love: ever devoted to the Lord, who have crossed beyond samsara, foremost in the teaching of the Satvata-tantras, masters of all conclusions, rasikas ever bestowing the rasa of bhakti, ornaments [of the world] who drive out unbelief."

278What can I say of Sri Narottama's deeds?
He visited all the tirthas, a brahmachari from boyhood!

279Thus [it is said] in the same work: "A brahmachari from boyhood, who has seen all the tirthas, the best of the highest bhagavatas — Srila Narottama Dasa."

280Who does not know his power?
He was born drawn by Krishna Chaitanya.

281Narottama was born on the full-moon day of the month of Magha;
day by day he grew like the moon.

282At home he became mature in every respect,
absorbed day and night in the virtues of Sri Krishna Chaitanya.

283By the Lord's will he is the embodiment of prema-bhakti;
great royal wealth does not touch his heart at all.

284Soon he thinks day and night:
"How can I leave home and become a renunciant?"

285To Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Nityananda, Advaita and their associates
he offers his prayers, and tears stream from both his eyes.

286In the guise of a dream the Lord with His associates appeared to him,
comforted His beloved Narottama and calmed him.

287Suddenly a man came from the king of Gauda,
and his father and uncle went to the court in Gauda.

288Taking this opportunity he deceived the guards
and somehow took leave of his mother.

289His mother, most virtuous, was named Narayani;
her life was in her son; what can be said of her ways?

290The mother lives carefree, cherishing her son,
and does not know that her son will leave home.

291Narottama, meanwhile, in deep secrecy
set out, meditating on the feet of the Lord.

292How fresh his youth, how handsome he is!
On the full-moon day of Kartika he left home.

293Having visited many tirthas he came to Vrindavana
and became a disciple of Lokanatha Gosvami.

294On the full moon of the month of Shravana, at an auspicious moment,
Lokanatha accepted Narottama as his disciple.

295The life of Sri Lokanatha is truly wondrous;
since the occasion has come, I shall say a little of it.

296He lived in the village of Talakhaida in the land of Yashohara;
his mother was Sita, his father Padmanabha Chakravarti.

297Thus it is said by the ancients: "I worship Sri Lokanatha Prabhu, the son of Padmanabha, possessed of the wealth of the service of Sri Radha-vinoda alone."

298Padmanabha was very dear to Prabhu Advaita;
Lokanatha is the son of this old brahmana.

299Even at home Lokanatha always lived detached;
giving up everything, he came to the Lord in Navadvipa.

300Prabhu Gaurachandra showed him great mercy
and ordered him to go to Vrindavana quickly.

301Such an order was not without purpose:
the Lord was soon going to accept sannyasa.

302Having become a sannyasi He would go to Vrindavana —
that is why He wished to send him ahead.

303Lokanatha understood these hints:
in a day or two the Lord would accept sannyasa.

304"His beautiful curling hair will be seen no more —
how will those who love Him keep their lives?"

305At these thoughts alone he was thrown into turmoil
and, weeping, bowed at the Lord's feet.

306The all-knowing Lord embraced Lokanatha,
secretly comforted him and sent him off.

307Lokanatha gave himself to the Lord's feet,
bowed to the Lord's associates and departed.

308In sorrow he wandered through many tirthas,
and after some time he came to Vrindavana.

309The Lord, meanwhile, who is subservient to His devotees, having accepted sannyasa,
went to Nilachala and saw Nilachala-chandra.

310From there the Lord set out on His tour of the South;
hearing of this, Lokanatha went south.

311From the South the Lord came to Vrindavana;
hearing of this, Lokanatha went to Vraja.

312From Vrindavana the Lord left for Prayaga,
while Lokanatha, arriving in Vraja, was in despair.

313He resolved to set out for Prayaga in the morning,
but in a dream the Lord comforted him and kept him in Vrindavana.

314Lokanatha could not transgress the Lord's command
and lived unknown in the forests of Vraja.

315After some time he met
Rupa and Sanatana — what joy in Vrindavana!

316Sri Gopala Bhatta and all the other associates of the Lord —
who can tell how close he was to them all?

317His affection for Bhugarbha is known to the world:
only their bodies were different from Lokanatha's.

318Prabhu Lokanatha, accomplished in every way,
served Sri Govinda and the other [Deities] for some time.

319Ever overwhelmed with prema, the very limit of renunciation,
he is renowned in the world for his wondrous greatness.

320In the Hari-bhakti-vilasa Gosani Sanatana
named him in the mangalacharana.

321Thus [it is said there]:
"Kashishvara shines in Krishna's forest, and so does Sri Krishnadasa with Lokanatha."33

322And at the beginning of the book Sri Vaishnava-toshani
he named him for the sake of blessing.

323Thus [it is said there]: "I praise those dear to Vrindavana, who have taken shelter at Sri Govinda's feet: the illustrious Kashishvara, Lokanatha and Sri Krishnadasa."

324Lokanatha wandered constantly through Vraja,
rejoicing at the sight of the places of Krishna's pastimes.

325Near Chhatravana there is a village named Umrao;
there Sri Kishori-kunda is of incomparable beauty.

326In that place he lived for some time in solitude,
and in his mind was the longing to serve a Deity.

327The Lord knew that Lokanatha was yearning,
and came in another form, bringing a Deity.

328Telling Him His name — Radha-vinoda — He handed Him over
and at that very moment vanished from there.

329Lokanatha Gosani reflects to himself:
"Who gave me such a Deity, and where has he gone?"

330Seeing Lokanatha troubled by his thoughts,
Sri Radha-vinoda says to him with a smile:

331"I live in the forest by this village of Umrao;
here, at this Kishori-kunda, is My place.

332Seeing your longing, I too grew restless:
who will bring Me? — and I came Myself.

333Quickly give Me something to eat."
Hearing this, he sheds tears of prema without cease.

334With great joy he quickly cooked and fed Him,
made a bed of flowers and laid Him down to rest.

335For some time he fanned Him with leaves,
and with joy in his heart massaged His feet.

336Body, mind and life he gave to the Lord's feet
and became absorbed in drinking the nectar of the sweetness of that form.

337He quickly made a cloth bag —
it became like a temple for Radha-vinoda.

338That bag became wondrously beautiful;
he keeps it always on his chest, like a necklace.

339The villagers want to build him a hut,
but nothing pleases Lokanatha except the roots of trees.

340Supremely detached, he accepted only
what was needed to keep himself alive — others cannot understand this.

341After staying for some time at the kunda, he came to Vrindavana;
all the Gosvamis lovingly kept him with them.

342For some time he lived in supreme bliss,
but then the burning fire of separation overwhelmed him:

343Sanatana, Rupa and the others passed from sight;
his condition then cannot be described.

344Day and night he weeps for the virtues of Sanatana and Rupa;
only by the Lord's will does life remain in his body.

345At that very time Narottama came there
and joyfully served his guru as is fitting.

346Pleased with his service, he gave him the mantra of initiation
and showed Narottama boundless mercy.

347Sri Gopala Bhatta and all the other wise ones
regard Narottama as their second life.

348There he received the name "Sri Thakura Mahashaya";
all of Sri Jiva's love for him cannot be described.

349Srinivasa Acharya met him in that same place;
there is no end to the joy he felt.

350There too took place the meeting with Shyamananda;
of him I shall tell a little here.

351He lived in the village of Dandeshvara, prosperous in every way;
his mother was Sri Durika, his father Sri Krishna Mandala.

352The best of the Sadgopa caste and most virtuous,
[the father] saw his all in Krishna and greatly loved the devotees.

353The virtues of Sri Krishna Mandala and Durika
cannot be described for fear of the bulk of the book.

354Formerly [the family] lived at Dharenda-Bahadurpur;
respectable people say that Shyamananda was born there.

355Mandala lacked nothing in any way,
[but] after [his] sons and daughters had died, Shyamananda was born.

356Shyamananda was born at a most auspicious moment;
whoever saw him even once was filled with great joy.

357Seeing the radiance of his son, Krishna [Mandala] says to his wife:
"Take care of him — may Krishna protect him."

358The women of the village say again and again:
"For now let his name be Duhkhiya (the Wretched One)."34

359His mother and father raised him with anxiety;
that is why he was first named Duhkhi.

360The joy at the ceremonies
of his first feeding with rice and his first haircut cannot be told.

361He never mixed with other boys;
grammar and the rest he learned in a short time.

362Day by day he grows, and all rejoice to see it;
truly wondrous inclinations appeared in him.

363The lives of Gaura, Nityananda, Advaita and their associates
he listens to attentively from the lips of Vaishnavas,

364constantly sings their virtues,
and tears flow from his eyes like the stream of a river.

365He always drinks the nectar of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna
and is most diligent in serving his father and mother.

366Seeing that their son had come of age, his parents say:
"Take initiation in the Krishna mantra from whomever you wish."

367Hearing them, he says with joined palms:
"My master is Hridaya Chaitanya in Ambika.

368He is a branch of Prabhu Gauridasa Pandita,
who is dear to Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda;

369in his house the two brothers dwell in person.35
If I receive permission, I shall go there and become his disciple.

370If you say, 'How will you travel to a distant land?' —
I have thought of a way:

371many people from our country go to bathe in the Ganga;
if I go with them, there is nothing to fear.

372Be kind, both of you, and give me your permission,
so that all my desires may be fulfilled."

373Hearing their son's words they rejoiced
and, by the Lord's will, gave their son leave.

374Having taken leave, he came to Ambika-nagara;
Sri Hridaya Chaitanya, seeing him, was pleased

375and asked: "What is your name? Why have you come?"
He laid everything before his master's feet.

376Mercy arose in Sri Hridaya Chaitanya:
his former name was Duhkhi — he gave him the name Krishnadasa.

377That the name "Shyamananda" would be revealed in Vrindavana
he indicated by a hint, and the wise understood.

378He became known as Duhkhi Krishnadasa
and was appointed to serve his guru's Deity.

379Sri Hridaya Chaitanya Thakura, full of prema,
was greatly pleased with his service.

380Having made him his disciple, he offered him to the Lord's feet;
Sri Shyamananda's desire was fulfilled.

381Thus [it is said] in the Shyamananda-shataka: "He whom people on earth glorify as the beloved disciple of Hridayananda and as the dear disciple's disciple of Sri Subala, the Lord's friend — may that illustrious crest-jewel of the kings of rasikas shine day and night in my heart, awakening a taste for the intimate sports of Sri Radha's Beloved."36

382After some days [Hridaya Chaitanya], kind to Shyamananda,
commanded him: "Go quickly to Vrindavana."

383Hearing these words, he pleads in distress:
"Prabhu, order me to stay near you."

384Hridaya Chaitanya embraced him again
and, overcome by prema, said: "Go to Vrindavana."

385Duhkhi Krishnadasa, weeping bitterly,
bowed at his master's feet and took his leave.

386At the sight of Prabhu Nityananda and Chaitanya37
tears of prema welled up from both his eyes.

387Lamenting long, he bowed to the ground
and took leave of the Lord's associates.

388He saw Navadvipa and other places
and everywhere begged for the great wealth of prema-bhakti.

389Crying "Sri Gauda-mandala!" he wails aloud;
tears pour down his face and chest.

390The associates of Nityananda, Advaita and Chaitanya —
uttering their names, he weeps without end.

391Again and again he prays to the Lord:
"May Sri Gauda-mandala be merciful to me!"

392Who can fathom the mind of a great soul?
In passing I shall tell why he prays to Gauda.

393Everyone calls Sri Gauda-mandala a chintamani:
by the mercy of Sri Gauda all desires are fulfilled.

394Thus [it is said] in a song (a prayer of Thakura Mahashaya):38
"He whose wealth and treasure are Gauranga's two feet
knows the essence of the rasa of bhakti.
He into whose ears Gauranga's sweet pastimes have entered —
his heart has become pure.

395In whoever utters Gauranga's name prema arises;
I give myself up for him.
To whoever weeps over Gauranga's virtues the eternal pastimes are revealed:
such a person is qualified for bhakti.

396He who knows Gauranga's associates as eternally perfect
goes to the son of the king of Vraja.
He who knows the land of Sri Gauda-mandala as a chintamani
obtains residence in the land of Vraja.

397He who plunges into the waves of the ocean of the rasa of prema for Gaura
is an intimate of Radha and Madhava.
Whether he lives at home or in the forest — he who calls 'Ha Gauranga!',
his company Narottama begs for."

398Thus many great souls sing the glories of Gauda;
Shyamananda constantly meditates on the land of Gauda.

399At his master's command, full of eagerness,
having seen many tirthas, he soon came to Vrindavana.

400In Vrindavana he performs a wondrous sadhana;
at the sight of it everyone's eyes and hearts are gladdened.

401He gave great joy to Shyamasundara —
and in Vrindavana he received a new name: "Shyamananda".39

402Sri Jiva Gosvami, seeing his fine conduct,
kept him by his side and taught him the books of bhakti.

403All the Lord's associates who lived in Vrindavana
rejoiced at heart on seeing Shyamananda.

404All that Shyamananda does in Vrindavana
is only at the command of his gurudeva.

405Hearing of Sri Shyamananda's fine life,
Sri Hridaya Chaitanya here [in Gauda] rejoiced at heart.

406He writes in a letter to Sri Jiva Gosvami:
"I have entrusted my disciple Duhkhi Krishnadasa to you.

407Fulfil all the desires of his heart,
and after some time send him back here."

408And to Shyamananda he constantly sends word:
"Know that Sri Jiva is my second self.

409Be careful in acquiring the jewel of bhakti,
and see that you commit no offence against the Vaishnavas."

410Thus he always admonishes his disciple;
by the guru's grace Shyamananda is fortunate.

411After some time, coming to Gauda by the Lord's will,
he accepted Sri Murari and others as disciples in Utkala.40

412These matters are not set out in detail here;
boundless is his love with Sri Narottama.

413In Vrindavana Narottama bathes in the bliss of prema;
by the Lord's will he came again to Gauda.

414How he came to Gauda —
all of that will be described in detail.

415Narottama's disciple named Sri Vasanta,
born in a brahmana family, a great poet and a learned man,

416described in a song something of how Sri Narottama
went to Gauda, Vraja and Utkala.

417Thus [it is said] in a song (in any raga):
"Prabhu Narottama is a treasury of virtues;
his most tender body surpasses a golden lotus —
I do not know which creator fashioned it!

418Mad with prema for Gora, giving up royal enjoyments,
he is in supreme bliss in Vrindavana;
having found the priceless treasure, he gave himself
to the feet of Prabhu Lokanatha.

419Lokanatha mercifully accepted him as his own,
and he set out for Gauda;
having toured Sri Gauda and visited the city of Nilachala,
he entered Gauda once more.

420How much favour the Lord's associates showed him!
What wondrous songs he revealed!
Says this servant Vasanta:
he mercifully delivered the unbelievers and the asuras."

421Thus all have described [his life] in various ways;
now hear what I shall say.

422When Narottama came to Gauda,
Prabhu Lokanatha gave the command:

423the service of the Deities of Sri Gauranga and Krishna,
service to the Sri Vaishnavas, and the Lord's sankirtana.

424As he was commanded, so he applied himself:
he established the service of six beautiful Deities.

425With all earnestness he is always absorbed in their service;
the very sound of those names soothes the heart.

426Thus [it is said] in a verse of his: "Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Sri Krishna, Vrajamohana, Radha-ramana, O Radha, Radha-kanta — obeisance to You!"41

427Who can tell how pure his conduct was,
serving the Sri Vaishnavas with body, mind and words?

428Truly wondrous are his constant festivals of sankirtana;
in that ocean of happiness all bathe, down to the lowliest.

429Gauranga's dear associates in Gauda
all rejoice at heart on seeing Narottama.

430Sri Jahnava Devi, the daughter of Surya Pandita,
the beloved of Nityananda, worshipped in the world,

431expert in bestowing the jewel of prema-bhakti,
is pleased at the very name "Sri Thakura Mahashaya".

432Seeing his extraordinary prema and strong renunciation,
Sri Jahnava Devi was overwhelmed with great bliss.

433Coming mercifully to the village of Sri Kheturi,
she gave everyone her darshan and gladdened them.

434How many favours Srimati Jahnava Devi showed —
how can I, a worthless wretch, describe them?

435Sri Thakura Mahashaya is supremely generous;
whomever he favoured attained every perfection.

436By the Lord's will he accepted many disciples:
Ramakrishna Chakravarti, Ganganarayana,

437Santosha and others — all became noble on the path of bhakti;
all of Sri Narottama's deeds are extraordinary.

438Sri Govinda Kaviraja, full of joy,
described something of his life in a song.

439Thus [it is said] in a song:
"Glory, glory, glory to Thakura Narottama,
the great king of prema-bhakti,
whose minister, one with him in body,
is Ramachandra Kaviraja!42

440Prema is the jewel of his crown, his ornaments the succession of bhavas,
with which every limb of his shines;
on the royal throne in Kheturi he sits,
and with him the assembly of devotees.

441The books of Sanatana and Rupa, the Srimad Bhagavata
he examines day after day:
Radha-Madhava, the brilliant rasa of the Couple —
the essence of supreme bliss.

442Enraptured by Sri Sankirtana as his only enjoyment,
he knows neither dharma nor adharma;
yoga, charity, vows and the rest flee in fear,
karma and knowledge weep.

443The shastras — the Bhagavata and the others that give the treasure of bhakti —
he himself honours;
the Sankhyas, the Mimamsakas, the logicians and their like
tremble at the sight of his might.

444The thieves who are non-devotees flee far from him
and do not show themselves nearby;
to the poor and lowly he gave the treasure of bhakti —
only Govindadasa is left deprived."

445Govinda, Sri Ramachandra's younger brother, is full of bhakti;
learned in all the shastras, he is praised by all as a poet.

446Sri Jiva, Sri Lokanatha and others in Vrindavana
felt supreme bliss drinking the nectar of his songs.

447There they all gave him the title Kaviraja,
and the Gosanis of Vraja praised him greatly in verse.

448Thus [it is said]: "The fragrance of the garland of verses connected with the moon Krishna, brought from the sandal mountain — Sri Govinda, the king of poets — by the playful spring breeze, has intoxicated the bees that take shelter at the feet of the celestial tree, the illustrious Jiva, and has caused wonder to all in the forests of Vraja. What could be higher?"

449Sri Jiva Gosvami in letters from Vraja
again and again asks him to send the nectar of his songs.

450Sri Govinda Kaviraja, at the Gosvami's command,
sends his nectarean songs to Vrindavana.

451These matters will be set out more fully later;
Sri Govinda Kaviraja is the life of all.

452Whatever he describes becomes the highest nectar;
Narottama, the Kaviraja and others relish it.

453Whatever the wise ask him to describe,
he describes at once with a mind full of supreme joy.

454King Harinarayana, foremost among Vaishnavas,
knows no one but Ramachandra.

455How he became a disciple and whom he himself made disciples —
of this I have not been able to tell here.

456Harinarayana made a request to the Kaviraja,
and he composed for him a song on the deeds of Sri Rama.

457Thus [it is said] in a song (in any raga):
"Glory, glory to Rama, to Rama, the joy of the Raghus,
the beloved husband of Janaka's daughter,
whose virtues are sung without end
by gods, men, monkeys, birds and night-roamers!

458Glory, glory to Him, [dark] like durva grass, like a fresh cloud,
lotus-eyed, steadfast in battle;
at His right are the arrows, in His left hand the bow,
He is deep as millions of oceans.

459Bharata holds His sandals,
Bharata's younger brother does not let go of the umbrella and the chamara;
Shiva, the Four-faced One, Sanaka and Sanatana
stand before Him with joined palms.

460With joy in his heart the son of the Wind
serves the feet of [the elder brother of] Bharata.
Govindadasa has firmly settled in his heart:
[Rama is] Harinarayana's chosen God."43

461So, with the permission of Sri Santosha Datta,
he composed the drama named Sangita-madhava.

462Wondrously is the purvaraga of Radha and Krishna depicted in it;
hearing it, Santosha Datta was filled with supreme joy.

463In passing I shall tell something of Santosha —
by this account the ears, mind and heart are satisfied.

464On the bank of the Padmavati there is a capital —
the beautiful town of Gopalpura.

465There live King Krishnananda Datta
and Sri Purushottama Datta, great of soul.

466The elder is Purushottama, the younger Krishnananda;
the love of these two brothers is the people's joy.

467Sri Krishnananda's son is Srila Narottama,
whose incomparable life I spoke of before.

468Sri Purushottama's son, named Santosha,
is Krishnananda's nephew, skilful in affairs,

469a minister of the king of Gauda, adept at caring for the subjects,
very powerful: others are subordinate to him.

470In every way he increases everyone's joy;
very learned, he is always engaged in discussions of the shastras.

471He is Sriman Narottama's brother and disciple,
pure in serving the guru, Krishna and the Vaishnavas.

472Thus [it is said] in the drama Sangita-madhava: "Sri Santosha Datta — a resident of the town of Gopalpura on the bank of the Padmavati, a great minister of the lord of Gauda, the best son of Sri Purushottama Datta, the younger cousin and disciple of the best of the Dattas, Sri Narottama Mahashaya — by him [at his wish] the drama Sangita-madhava, on the purvaraga and other pastimes of Sri Radha and Madhava, following Their manifest pastimes in a worldly manner, has been composed and, honoured with many gifts of jewels and other things, presented."44

473And again: "He who, binding Sri Radhika and Madhava together within with the cords — the qualities — of prema, brought Them outside through the lotus of his heart, manifestly, for the good of the world, and in his own home served Them, offering everything — who here is more pious than Santosha Datta? Enough [said]!"

474And again: "Oh! In Sri Gauranga, in the Beloved of Vraja, in Radha-ramana, in Radha-kanta — the manifest forms of Hari! What an assembly, what beauty, what service to the guru there was! Ah, apart from Santosha there is no other abode of joy."45

475Seeing the truly wondrous deeds of Santosha Datta,
people vie with one another in singing Santosha's virtues.

476Some say: "Someone must be helping him,
otherwise such wealth of bhakti cannot be obtained."

477Others say: "The Kaviraja and Narottama must be
his helpers; hence his incomparable intelligence."

478Thus [it is said] in the drama Sangita-madhava: "He whose helpers are always the illustrious Kaviraja and Narottama — what wonder is it that he has such intelligence?"

479The wondrous way of bhakti of Sri Santosha Datta
I cannot unfold here because of the bulk of the book.

480With Govinda Kaviraja he has a great friendship:
in everything they are one, only their bodies differ.

481In the village of Sri Kheturi, with all these dear ones,
the Kaviraja and Narottama spend their time joyfully.

482I have told briefly of the relationship of these two;
from hearing of it love for Krishna is born.

483How Sri Ramachandra served his chosen Deity
I shall relate in detail further on.

484And now I shall tell what I mentioned before —
the story of Sri Gokulananda Chakravarti.

485An associate of Sri Krishna Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
is the brahmana Haridasa Acharya, who removes misfortunes,

486expert in bestowing the great jewel of prema-bhakti,
day and night intoxicated with the rasa of sankirtana.

487His sons are Gokulananda and Shridasa;
from infancy they drew all hearts.

488Without effort they became expert in all the shastras,
ever intoxicated with the bliss of sankirtana.

489What shall I say of the greatness of Sri Gokulananda,
the very limit of Srinivasa Acharya's mercy?

490As his father commanded Gokula, so he did:
he became a disciple and was devoted to his guru's feet.

491Such too is the way of bhakti of the most learned Shridasa;
you will learn this wondrous story in detail further on.

492Srinivasa Acharya, supremely merciful,
spends his time happily with these disciples.

493He always teaches the truth of bhakti,
intoxicating the world with the virtues of Sri Krishna Chaitanya.

494Srinivasa Acharya is the Lord's beloved servant;
his fame has filled the earth and the sky.

495Captivating is the story of Srinivasa's birth and the rest;
the Vaishnavas always long to hear it.

496I have not understood the Vaishnavas' design at all:
they commanded such a fool as me to describe it.

497Holding in my heart the strength of their command,
I shall tell what I can — listen with joy.

498Whoever wishes to hear of Srinivasa's life,
with him Gaura, the son of the king of Vraja, is well pleased.

499Whoever rejoices at heart on hearing this,
to him Prabhu Nityananda and Sri Advaita are merciful.

500Prabhu Gadadhara, Srivasa and the other devotees
give the wealth of bhakti to whoever is attached to this.

501But whoever has no faith in his life,
for him all of this leads to utter ruin.

502Listen, all of you, to the life of Srinivasa —
without effort all your desires will be fulfilled.

503And whatever else I describe here in passing —
hearing all of it, your great joy will increase.

504It is so sweet that at its mere touch upon the ear
even those turned away will easily turn [to the Lord].

505Again and again I beg you, listeners:
relish this book without cease.

506The wise named this book Bhakti-ratnakara;
in it are various "waves", most captivating.

507Placing on your head the lotus feet of the assembly of the Sri devotees,
dive always into this Bhakti-ratnakara.46

508Everyone says that bhakti is the property of the devotees;
if the devotees give it, you obtain this jewel of bhakti.

509Glory, glory to Bhakti-devi! Be merciful to the wretched:
no desire is fulfilled without the touch of bhakti.

510Even if for many lives one performs various sadhanas,
the wealth of bhakti at Krishna's feet still remains out of reach.

511Whoever longs to obtain that wealth at the Lord's feet,
let him relish the rasa of bhakti without cease.

512Keep the jewel of bhakti carefully in your heart:
all the shastras sing that bhakti is the chief of all.

513Thus [it is said]: "Liberation is easily obtained through knowledge, enjoyment through the merit of sacrifices and the like; but this Hari-bhakti is hard to attain even by thousands of sadhanas."47

514Who is able to tell the greatness of bhakti?
To relish the rasa of bhakti Chaitanya descended.

515Would that I could take upon myself all the troubles of such an Avatara:
He made the lowest worthy of bhakti for Krishna!

516Otherwise [Krishna] keeps this jewel of bhakti hidden
and never gives it, putting people off with enjoyment and liberation.

517Thus [it is said] in the Srimad Bhagavatam: "O King, Mukunda was for you and for the Yadus the Lord, guru, Deity, beloved, head of the family, and at times even a servant. Yes, that is so, my dear: Bhagavan Mukunda grants liberation to those who worship Him, but bhakti-yoga only rarely."48

518Bhakti, inaccessible even to Brahma — who attains it?
It became easy to attain by the mercy of Krishna Chaitanya.

519Prabhu Nityananda is non-different from Balarama;
the avatara of Maha-Vishnu bears the name Sri Advaita.

520Ah, ah, how wondrous the mercy of these two!
They filled the world with an ocean of bhakti.

521Sri Gadadhara Pandita and the other shaktis of the Lord —
to whom did they not mercifully give bhakti for Krishna?

522Srivasa and all the other devotees of the Lord
distributed the wealth of bhakti in great bliss.

523Who can describe the virtues of Gora, the giver of bhakti?
He gives it Himself and makes everyone give it.

524Placing devotees in various places,
He made known the supreme and rarest bhakti.

525To Rupa and Sanatana He gave the western country,
and there they revealed [bhakti] on the authority of the shastras of bhakti.

526They wrote the book Sri Hari-bhakti-vilasa,
in which hundreds of thousands of limbs of bhakti are revealed,

527and the mighty book Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu,
on hearing which the devotees' hearts are filled with joy.

528These two great warriors are the beloved of the Lord and of the devotees;
by merely remembering them one obtains bhakti for Krishna.

529Sri Jiva Gosvami and all the other great souls,
by revealing the shastras of bhakti, conquered the world.

530Who can describe the virtues of Sri Jiva Gosani,
upon whom rests the full mercy of Sanatana Gosvami?

531The life of Sri Sanatana is truly wondrous;
he loves the Srimad Bhagavatam beyond measure.

532In his early youth, in a dream, a venerable brahmana
with joy in his heart gives him the Srimad Bhagavatam.

533On waking, Sanatana was agitated —
[and in waking life] that same brahmana lovingly handed him the Srimad Bhagavatam.

534Having received the Sri Bhagavata, with great joy at heart
my master sank into the ocean of the nectar of prema.

535How he relished the meaning of the Srimad Bhagavatam
he revealed in the Sri Vaishnava-toshani.

536Of Sri Sanatana's past I shall speak briefly;
Sri Jiva Gosvami set it out in detail in the Toshani.

537Thus [it is said] in the Laghu-toshani: "Those who in early youth received the Sri Bhagavata in a dream, and in the morning, awake, from the very brahmana they had seen in the dream,

538and sank into the great ocean of the nectar of prema for Bhagavan — this writing is truly theirs, of those called Sri Sanatana.

539Having offered it, Jiva, whose life is their feet, wishing to say something more, now offers this."49

540Seven ancestors of Sri Jiva Gosvami are known;
beginning from the first, I shall name them all.

541Sri Sarvajna, named Jagadguru, a king among brahmanas,
greatly venerated, [a follower] of the Yajurveda, of the Bharadvaja lineage,

542a teacher of all the Vedas, of great prowess,
was king of the land of Karnata, and none was his equal.

543All kings always honoured him;
how wealthy he was — who can tell?

544His son Aniruddha-deva was like Indra;
his fame, the best of all, rivalled the moon.

545Honoured by kings, a knower of the Vedas, wealthy,
he had two queens, famed on earth.

546He had two sons, Rupeshvara and Harihara,
whose many virtues were known everywhere.

547The elder son, Rupeshvara, was expert in the shastras;
the younger, Harihara, was highly skilled in arms.

548Having divided the kingdom and entrusted it to the two of them,
the father attained the abode of Sri Krishna.

549After some time, gathering men,
the younger seized the elder's kingdom.

550Having lost his kingdom, Rupeshvara with his wife
came on eight horses to the eastern country.

551Enjoying the friendship of Sri Shikhareshvara,
Rupeshvara-deva settled there.

552Sri Rupeshvara's son was named Padmanabha;
he was beautiful and incomparable in all virtues.

553In the study of the Yajurveda with its angas and the rest
his wondrous fame was known to the world.

554How wondrous is the life of Padmanabha-deva!
He always rejoiced in love for Sri Jagannatha.

555From the land of King Shikhara, Padmanabha
came to the bank of the Ganga, wishing to settle there.

556The great soul settled in the village of Navahatta,
which all people call Naihati.50

557There Padmanabha-deva, with great joy in his heart,
diligently worships the form of Sri Purushottama.

558Performing sacrifices and festivals, he was in supreme bliss;
eighteen daughters and five sons were born to him:

559Sri Purushottama, Jagannatha, Narayana,
Murari and Mukunda — these five sons.

560The eldest was Purushottama, the youngest of all Mukunda;
skilful in everything, with the best of virtues.

561Sri Mukunda-deva's son was Sri Kumara,
the lamp of the brahmana family, supremely pure in conduct.

562He always performs sacrifices and other rites in seclusion
and greatly fears the touch of people of bad conduct.

563If ever he chances to see a yavana,
he performs atonement and takes no food.

564Anxiety arose in his mind on account of his kinsmen,
and he at once left the village of Navahatta.

565With his people he went in haste to the land of Vanga
and settled in the village of Bakla-Chandradvipa.51

566In Yashohara there is a village named Fatehabad;
for his journeys back and forth he made a dwelling there.

567Many children were born to Kumara-deva;
among them three sons, the life of the Vaishnavas:

568Sanatana, Rupa and Sri Vallabha — these three;
they brought their lineage great honour in this world and the next.

569Thus [it is said] in the same work: "He whose triple wish-fulfilling creeper — the tongue — streaming nectar in the beautiful pada-krama, dances like a bee; whose feet were honoured by the assembly of kings — the king of Karnata, Sri Sarvajna Jagadguru, chief of the Bharadvaja lineage, shone on earth.

570The son of that king, while he ruled the earth — whose fame rivalled the moon, equal in might to the lord of the gods, honoured by all kings, the sole repository of the whole Yajurveda, wealthy — became famous on earth by the name Aniruddha-deva.

571From the two queens of that renowned king were born sons, treasuries of virtue, named Rupeshvara and Harihara; the first, impelled by his own nature, attained great strength in the many shastras, the other in arms.

572On the day of his departure to the abode of the Enemy of Madhu the father divided his kingdom and gave it to Rupeshvara and Harihara; but the younger, Harihara, drove from his kingdom his elder, Rupeshvara, the ornament of a noble family.

573Sri Rupeshvara-deva, thus deprived of his kingdom by enemies, went gradually with his wife on eight horses to the eastern country; living there happily in friendship in the domain of Shikhareshvara, the blessed one begot a son, a treasury of virtues, named Sri Padmanabha.

574On whose tongue the Yajurveda with its angas and all the Upanishads in their fullness clearly danced, whose heart rejoiced in love for Jagannatha — into whose ears has [the fame] of that son of King Rupeshvara not come?

575The crown of virtues, giving up the wish to live in the land of Shikhara and eager to dwell on the bank of the shining celestial river, the accomplished Padmanabha, honoured by King Danujamardana, in time settled in Navahatta.52

576While he worshipped there the form of Sri Purushottama with splendid festivals, five sons were born to him together with eighteen daughters: the first Purushottama, then Jagannatha, the steadfast Narayana, Srila Murari of excellent virtues, and the accomplished Sriman Mukunda.

577From that Mukunda was born the best of brahmanas named Sriman Kumara; meeting with some hostility, he went with his family to Vanga. Among his sons were born three, dearest to the great Vaishnavas, who made their lineage greatly honoured both in this world and in the next."

578Sanatana, Rupa and Sri Vallabha are kings among devotees;
the eldest of all is Sanatana, his younger brother Sri Rupa,

579and the youngest of all is Sri Vallabha, full of prema;
Sri Jiva Gosvami is his son.

580How the three brothers lived at home
I cannot describe for fear of the bulk of the book.

581Sanatana and Rupa were great ministers in every respect:
the king heard of them from the lips of respectable people.

582The king of Gauda, a yavana ruling many lands,
summoned Sanatana and Rupa and gave them the burden of government.

583For fear of the mlechchhas they accepted the post,
and through their efforts his kingdom grew.

584The delighted king gave them separate estates,
and they enjoyed them, paying only a small tax.

585They settled in Gauda, in the village of Ramakeli;
the very limit of wealth, a truly wondrous splendour!

586To the assembly of Sanatana and Rupa, who were like Indra,
knowers of the shastras come from various lands.

587Singers, musicians, dancers and poets
from every country are constantly in their service.

588They spend a great deal of money without cease,
and no one is ever left without honour.

589Both always occupy themselves with all the shastras
and refute and establish [doctrines] without effort.

590An interpretation of the nyaya-sutras that anyone made of his own
is established only when Sanatana and Rupa have heard it.

591So all, convinced in every way,
joyfully sing the virtues of Sanatana and Rupa.

592The fame of their virtues spread everywhere;
brahmanas came from Karnata and other lands.

593To the brahmanas from their native country Sanatana and Rupa
gave all of them places to live near the Ganga.

594The village where the community of Bhattas lives is called Bhattavati;
all there are knowers of the shastras, incomparable in all doctrines.

595With those brahmanas in the village of Ramakeli
they joyfully carry out all their worldly affairs.

596How Rupa and Sanatana honour
the communities of Vaishnavas cannot be described.

597How many brahmanas come from Navadvipa,
and how they honour them all, I cannot tell.

598Sri Sanatana's guru is Vidya-vachaspati;
from time to time he stayed in the village of Ramakeli.

599Under him [Sanatana] studied all the shastras;
what his devotion to his guru was cannot be told.

600In his commentary on the Tenth Canto Sanatana
wrote his guru's name for the sake of blessing.

601Thus [it is said] in the commentary on the Tenth Canto: "I bow to my gurus — Bhattacharya Sarvabhauma and Vidya-vachaspati — and to Vidya-bhushana, the ornament of the land of Gauda.

602I bow to Sri Paramananda Bhattacharya, the lover of rasa, and also to Ramabhadra and Vani-vilasa, my instructors."53

603How Sanatana and Rupa performed their sadhana —
who is able to tell of it in detail?

604Near their house, in a very secluded place,
there was a kadamba grove, and in it Radha-kunda and Shyama-kunda.

605There they meditate on the pastimes of Vrindavana;
they cannot restrain themselves, and tears flow from their eyes without cease.

606They are devoted to the service of the Deity Madanamohana;
how much shall I tell of their constant words of grief?

607Sri Krishna Chaitanya-chandra plays in Nadia,
and they always yearn to see Him.

608Thinking of how purely their fathers and grandfathers lived,
they condemn themselves in their hearts:

609"Our father, on seeing a yavana, performed atonement,
and we are in constant association with yavanas.

610Fawning, we go to the houses of yavanas" —
and therefore they consider themselves equal to mlechchhas.

611Their inner disposition is not at all like that,
but in this they consider themselves the lowest of the low.

612When they sink into the ocean of humility,
they consider themselves lower than mlechchhas and the rest.

613With the low-born there is always low dealing:
that is why they speak of themselves as low-born.

614Though kings among brahmanas, with great grief in their hearts
they never think of themselves as brahmanas.

615Such is the way of those on whom Sri Chaitanya's mercy rests:
never do they think of themselves as high.

616Always, with unchanging feeling, they consider themselves low;
Sri Krishna Chaitanya knows the truth about His devotee.

617The Purna-brahman, the eternal Sri Krishna Chaitanya —
as He humbles Himself, so no one else can.

618His devotees are always immersed in the rasa of humility;
what bliss lies in humility Gaura-raya knows.

619What was in the hearts of Sanatana and Rupa
Sri Krishna Chaitanya-chandra came to know.

620The Lord knows many ways to meet His devotee:
He came to Ramakeli on the way to Vrindavana.

621Hundreds of thousands of people run to see the Lord;
even yavanas joyfully sing the Lord's virtues.

622The hearts of Sanatana and Rupa overflow with joy;
coming secretly, they fall at the Lord's feet.

623How they pleaded, holding straw between their teeth —
at the mere telling of it everyone's heart breaks.

624The Lord, who loves His devotees, cannot restrain Himself:
at the humility of Sanatana and Rupa His soul weeps.

625In the book Chaitanya-charitamrita it is written:
"Give up this humility — your humility breaks My heart."54

626How they humbled themselves is partly told there;
for fear of the bulk of the book I do not write it here.

627The best in every respect, they humble themselves thus:
"low, mlechchhas, sinners" — so they revile themselves.

628The brahmanas were amazed, not understanding this secret:
the Lord was teaching people through His devotees.

629O brother! Who can understand the Lord's heart?
He is subject to His devotees, revealing the devotees' virtues.

630Through Ramananda He revealed the crushing of Kandarpa's pride,
through Damodara He revealed impartiality,

631through Haridasa He showed forbearance,
through Sanatana and Rupa He revealed humility.

632Control of the senses, impartiality, forbearance and humility —
these four utmost limits Sri Chaitanya revealed.55

633The humility of Sanatana and Rupa I cannot understand;
fools argue about it in various ways.

634Whoever wishes to go to the most terrible hell,
let him commit such offences as false arguments and the like.

635Having shown mercy to Sanatana and Rupa with their companions,
Gaurahari set out from Ramakeli.

636What happiness flooded Sanatana, Rupa
and Sri Vallabha, the three brothers, cannot be told.

637Keshava Chhatri and all the other wise men,
seeing the Lord, found the fulfilment [of their lives].

638Sri Jiva and others saw the Lord in secret;
this I heard from the lips of very old people.56

639Soon Sri Jiva's intellect became wondrous:
in grammar and the other shastras he attained great mastery.

640Sanatana and Rupa, looking upon their nephew,
show him great mercy and affection.

641Who can understand the life of Sri Jiva?
He thinks constantly of the beauty of the Lord's form.

642He studies the shastras with his teachers without cease;
seeing this, everyone is greatly pleased at heart.

643All say: "He was born from a portion of some god —
otherwise how could he have reached such mastery so soon?"

644"As beautiful as Sanatana, Rupa and Vallabha are,
so captivating is the beauty of Sri Jiva."

645Many things are said thus — I cannot describe them all;
would that I could take upon myself the troubles of such a Sri Jiva!

646Sanatana and Rupa, great ministers in every respect,
devised a way to leave their great affairs.

647To meet the Lord they performed a purashcharana
and appointed men to bring news of the Lord.

648First they cautiously sent off their households —
some to Chandradvipa, some to Fatehabad.

649Sri Rupa with Vallabha, boarding a boat,
joyfully went home with great wealth.

650All the wealth he distributed to brahmanas, Vaishnavas and others,
and, hearing that the Lord had gone to Vraja, set out.

651From Vrindavana the Lord came to Prayaga;
coming to Prayaga, Rupa and Vallabha met Him.

652In supreme bliss Gaurahari showed them mercy
and carefully sent them off quickly to Vrindavana.

653Sanatana conducted the royal affairs through other people,
while he himself at home occupied himself with examining the shastras:

654gathering twenty or thirty bhattacharyas and pandits,
he sits in assembly and discusses the Bhagavata.

655In the Chaitanya-charitamrita all this is described:
Sanatana went to Kashi and met the Lord.57

656Who can describe the mercy the Lord showed Sanatana,
from whose body He wiped away the dirt with His own hand?

657Kavi Karnapura, dear to the Lord, wrote a book
and told of the grace shown to Sanatana.

658Thus [it is said there]: "He who was the jewel ornament of the assembly of the lord of Gauda — the elder brother of Rupa — giving up flourishing wealth, took to wife the young Lakshmi of renunciation; within full of the rasa of bhakti, without in the guise of an avadhuta, like a great lake covered with moss, he gives joy to those who know him."

659[And again:] "As soon as He saw with His own eyes Sanatana arriving, the Lord, golden as a champaka, softened by boundless compassion, trembling, embraced him with His arms long as door-bolts."

660[And again:] "Seeing that in the course of time the accounts of the pastimes of Vrindavana had been lost, the Lord, in order to proclaim them especially, there and then sprinkled both Rupa and Sanatana with the nectar of His mercy."58

661Seeing the Lord's mercy towards Sanatana,
the devotees who lived in Kashi rejoiced at heart.

662At the Lord's command Sanatana went to Vraja,
while Rupa had left Vraja, and they did not meet.

663The Lord, meanwhile, having returned to Nilachala, after some days
began to long for Rupa and Sanatana.

664Sri Rupa with Vallabha, with joyful hearts,
hasten to Nilachala by way of Gauda.

665Sri Rupa's younger brother, the wise Vallabha —
Sri Gaurasundara gave him the name Anupama.

666He knows no one but Raghunatha
and is ever enraptured in the service of the Deity of Raghunatha.

667"Chaitanya Gosani is Sri Raghunatha Himself" —
and he considers himself blessed to have found such a Lord.

668What shall I say of the boundless greatness of Vallabha?
Sri Rupa came to Gauda with Vallabha.

669Sri Vallabha passed [from this world] on the bank of the Ganga;
after some days Rupa came to Nilachala.

670The bliss he felt on seeing in Nilachala
the Lord and His devotees — who can describe it?

671The mercy shown to Rupa
by Sri Chaitanya, Advaita and Nitai with their associates cannot be told.

672Having stayed for some time, at the Lord's command,
he set out for Vrindavana by way of Gauda.

673The wealth that remained in Gauda he had brought
and distributed to his kin, to brahmanas and to temples.

674Free of cares, he went to Vraja;
so it is written in the book Chaitanya-charitamrita.

675From Vrindavana Sri Sanatana Gosvami
set out for Niladri by the road through Jharikhanda.

676After some time he arrived in Nilachala;
seeing Sanatana, the Lord was overjoyed.

677With what wondrous love He brought him together with all the devotees!
Having kept him for some time, He sent him back to Vraja.

678In Vrindavana Sanatana met Sri Rupa;
this is described in detail in the Chaitanya-charitamrita.

679He upon whom falls even a particle of the mercy of these two
develops love for the feet of Sri Krishna Chaitanya.

680The son of a brahmana, the Gosvamis' family priest,
came to Vrindavana and received the mercy of both.

681Giving up the desire for wealth he had had, with a joyful heart
he became a disciple of Sanatana Gosvami.

682To this day his descendants in Madgram
know no one but Prabhu Sanatana.59

683Sanatana and Rupa, softened by compassion,
revealed the lost tirthas in Mathura-mandala.

684From Vrindavana [the Lord] drew Sri Jiva to Himself:
Sri Jiva Gosvami in Gauda grew restless.

685How Sri Jiva Gosvami went to Vrindavana —
of this truly wondrous story I shall tell a little.

686From the time the Gosvamis went to Vrindavana,
what came over Sri Jiva's heart!

687Various jewelled ornaments, fine garments,
wondrous beds and luxurious meals —

688all this he gave up, nothing pleases him,
and of kingdoms and worldly affairs he cannot bear to hear.

689Seeing Sri Jiva's conduct, respectable people
speak to one another with affection:

690"O brother! Among the sons of Kumara-deva
three are Vaishnavas and knowers of the shastras:

691Sanatana, Sri Rupa and Vallabha — these three
gave up everything and became renunciants.

692What wondrous renunciation — not a trace of attachment!
Such detachment is seen nowhere.

693On the bank of the Ganga Vallabha passed to the next world,
and at a young age Sri Jiva suffered great grief.

694Sri Jiva has no inclination for such wealth;
to tell how he fared breaks the heart.

695One day I saw him in solitude:
he is ceaselessly drowned in the tears of both his eyes."

696Another says: "O brother, that is true:
know for certain that Krishna's mercy rests on Sri Jiva.

697In his youth his heart is very deep;
the Srimad Bhagavatam he regards as his second life.

698He always swims in the ocean of happiness — talk of Krishna,
and no one dares out of fear to speak to him of anything else.

699One day I watched unseen:
crying 'Sri Krishna Chaitanya!' he fell unconscious.

700He rolls on the ground and cannot compose himself,
his face and chest are drenched by the streams from his eyes.

701How he laments, weeping and weeping —
