whose heart would not break at the sight of it?"

702A third says: "O brother, this is what I think:
Sri Jiva will very soon leave home."

703Someone says: "How will so tender a youth wander about?"
Another says: "Strong is his anuraga."

704Someone says: "He is the lamp of the brahmana family;
if he goes, all will be plunged into darkness."

705So all say many things with anxious hearts
and, unwilling to leave Sri Jiva, do not go home.

706In Sri Jiva's mind there is ceaselessly one thought:
"When shall I leave home?"

707One evening, sitting alone,
he chants the holy name and is bathed in tears.

708However hard he tries, he cannot restrain himself;
raising both arms, he says again and again:

709"O Prabhu Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Nityananda!
O ocean of mercy, Sri Advaitachandra!

710O merciful dear associates of the Lord!
Make such a fallen one as me worthy of your mercy!"

711So he speaks many times, his throat choking again and again;
the night passed, and there was no sleep in his eyes.

712By the will of the Lord, who loves His devotees,
Sri Jiva, dozing a little, has a dream.

713As he had seen in a dream in the village of Ramakeli,
so he sees Gaurachandra with His associates.

714In the midst of the sankirtana Gaura-raya dances,
intoxicating the world with prema unattainable even for Brahma.

715Hundreds of thousands of people come running from all sides;
the cry "Hari! Hari!" resounds on earth and in the sky.

716Having appeared thus, the Lord vanished;
on waking, Jiva was thrown into turmoil.

717Again sleep overcame Sri Jiva,
and Sri Jiva sees a wondrous dream.

718I shall tell that dream, but first a little of the past:
truly wondrous is the life of Sri Jiva.

719In his childhood Sri Jiva, with other boys,
knew no games but those connected with Sri Krishna.

720Making figures of Krishna and Balarama,
he would worship Them with flowers, sandal and the like.

721In various ornaments and garments They were very beautiful;
gazing at Them without blinking, he rejoiced at heart.

722Falling to the ground like a golden doll,
he bowed to Them and was bathed in tears.

723Offering Them various sweets with great care,
he would eat the prasada together with the boys.

724Apart from Krishna and Balarama nothing pleases him;
even alone, in solitude, he plays with the two of Them.

725Going to sleep, he keeps Them both on his chest,
and his father and mother cannot take Them away even in jest.

726Seeing such great love for Krishna and Balarama,
seeing such conduct in a child, all rejoiced.

727How Chaitanya and Nitai, from his childhood,
were subject to his love, They reveal in the dream:

728Lord Krishna and Balarama appeared before him in person —
dark and white, both abodes of bliss.

729The wondrous attire of the two enchants Kandarpa;
with the curves of Their bodies They intoxicate the three worlds.

730Having seen Them thus, he sees Them again golden:
They shine, surpassing pure gold.

731The fragrance of the bodies of both filled the three worlds,
and there is no one who can stay composed.

732Sri Jiva was amazed at heart
and gazes unblinking at the beauty of the two.

733Drowning in the tears of his long eyes,
he falls at the feet of the two Lords.

734The oceans of mercy, Gaura and Nityananda-raya,
placed Their lotus feet on Jiva's head.

735With great parental love They embrace him again
and speak nectarean words of comfort.

736Sri Gaurasundara, overcome with great prema,
entrusted him to the feet of Prabhu Nityananda.

737Nityananda says to Sri Jiva again and again:
"Let this Lord of Mine be everything to you."

738Having received such mercy from the Lord, he bowed again —
and seeing that both had vanished, he cannot calm himself.

739Waking, he sees that the night has passed;
on the pretext of study he set out for Navadvipa.

740The people of Chandradvipa thought to themselves:
"Sri Jiva will certainly go to Vrindavana."60

741Sri Jiva sent away the people accompanying him
and went from Fatehabad with one servant.

742Overcome with prema, how wondrously he walks along the road!
Seeing Sri Jiva, people say to one another:

743"Look, look, whose prince is this?
His body is captivating, the colour of a golden champaka.

744How wondrous the beauty of his face — it steals the soul!
How lovely his long eyes and nose!

745What brows, forehead, ears, what beautiful hair!
What cheeks and neck, what a wondrous chest!

746How the lotuses of his hands and the rows of his nails shine!
What a slender waist, what shanks, knees and feet!

747A wondrous tulasi-mala on his tender neck!
What a white, fine, beautiful sacred thread!

748O brother, would that I could take all his troubles upon myself!
I long to gaze at him without cease, filling my eyes."

749Someone says: "Brothers, looking at him
I do not know what is happening in my heart."

750Someone says: "This is what I think:
he will certainly accept sannyasa."

751So many speak with agitated hearts,
while Sri Jiva walks on, overcome with the highest prema.

752As he entered Navadvipa the word spread:
"The nephew of Sanatana and Sri Rupa has come!"

753Seeing Sri Jiva's conduct, the brahmanas and pandits —
whatever they asked him — were all amazed.

754Sri Jiva entered Navadvipa
and, seeing the beauty of Navadvipa, was amazed.

755Sixteen kroshas does beautiful Navadvipa extend;61
here and there are wells, flower gardens and ponds.

756Seeing the banks of the celestial river, the groves and sandbanks —
is there anyone whose heart would not be gladdened?

757Sri Jiva walks on in rapture,
and along the same road come several Vaishnavas.

758Seeing Sri Jiva, they all, rejoicing at heart,
hastened to the house of Sri Srivasa Pandita.

759There Prabhu Nityananda with His dear associates
sits enjoying the great bliss of prema.

760The Lord, smiling, says to Srivasa Pandita:
"It seems to Me that Sri Jiva will come."

761That Vaishnava says quietly to the Lord:
"Sri Jiva has come, Prabhu; he is outside the house."

762Hearing this, Prabhu Nityananda was delighted
and quickly had people bring in Sri Jiva.

763At the sight of the Lord Sri Jiva lost all composure
and cannot stem the streams of tears from both his eyes.

764How he humbled himself cannot be put into words;
he falls at the feet of Prabhu Nityananda.

765Prabhu Nityananda, overwhelmed with great parental love,
placed both His feet on Sri Jiva's head.

766He showed Sri Jiva the utmost mercy:
raising him from the ground, He embraced him tightly.

767In the rapture of prema the Lord says: "For your sake
I hastened here from Khardaha."

768Saying many such things, He calmed Sri Jiva
and had Srivasa and the other devotees show him mercy.

769Having kept him by His side in great joy,
He sends Sri Jiva off to the western country.

770At parting [Jiva] was in great distress;
Sri Jiva bowed at the feet of Nityananda.

771Placing His feet on Sri Jiva's head,
the Lord embraced him with great affection.

772The Lord says: "Go quickly to Vraja:
the Lord has given that place to your family."62

773With the Lord's permission Sri Jiva set out,
having honoured the feet of all the devotees.

774What affection Srivasa Pandita and the other bhagavatas
showed Sri Jiva cannot be described.

775From Navadvipa, his mind full of supreme bliss,
Sri Jiva Gosvami after some time reached Kashi.

776There lives Sri Madhusudana Vachaspati,
a teacher of all the shastras, like Brihaspati.

777Seeing Sri Jiva, he grew very fond of him
and, keeping him for some time, taught him Vedanta and the rest.

778The joy Vachaspati felt
at seeing the power of Sri Jiva's learning I have no power to tell.

779In Kashi everyone everywhere praises Sri Jiva:
"In nyaya, Vedanta and the other shastras there is no one like him."

780From Kashi Sri Jiva went to Vrindavana,
and there Rupa and Sanatana showed him mercy.

781Sanatana, Rupa and Sri Vallabha are three brothers;
to describe the lives of these three would have no end.

782How Raghunatha Dasa came from Sri Purushottama
to Vrindavana I cannot relate.

783Sanatana, Rupa and Raghunatha — these three...
Raghunatha's life and deeds are known to the world.

784Thus [it is said] in the Laghu-toshani: "The first is Srila Sanatana, his younger brother named Sri Rupa, then [the youngest] bearing the name Sriman Vallabha; turning away from royal power and obtaining the great mercy of Bhagavan Sri Krishna Chaitanya, they truly enjoyed the kingdom of the wealth of bhakti called prema for Murahara.

785He who was the youngest of all — my father — soon attained Sri Rama on the Ganga, while the elder [brothers] then came to Vrindavana; by them the hidden tirthas of Mathura were revealed, and bhakti for Sri Vrajaraja-nandana was raised high everywhere.

786Their friend, known on earth as Raghunatha Dasa, ever shines, whirling in the waves of the great ocean of the prema of Radha and Krishna; surpassing the splendour of all examples, he is held by the best of the worthy in the three worlds, to their amazement, to be equal in nature to those two."63

787Sanatana and Rupa live in Vrindavana;
what is in the hearts of the two of them — who knows but Krishna?

788To Sanatana and Rupa [the Lord] showed great mercy:
in the guise of a cowherd boy Gopala appeared before them.

789He gave them wondrous condensed milk — what more is there to say?
There is no limit to the happiness of Sanatana and Rupa.

790All that such Sanatana and Rupa, at the Lord's command,
wrote has spread throughout the world.

791Sri Rupa composed the Sri Hamsa-duta and other books,
Sanatana wrote the Bhagavatamrita and others.

792Having composed the Sri Vaishnava-toshani, Sanatana
ordered Sri Jiva to edit it.

793Receiving the order, Jiva composed the Laghu-toshani
and wrote there how he had done it.

794In [Shaka] 1476 the Brihat was completed,
in Shaka 1504 the Laghu.64

795Thus [it is said] in the same work: "In the guise of a cowherd boy Shriyuta Gopala Himself appeared to these two in the play of bringing them milk.

796Among the works of the younger of them are the poem Sri Hamsa-duta, the Srimad Uddhava-sandesha, and the Eighteen Metres;

797the hymns Utkalika-vallari, Govinda-virudavali, Premendu-sagara and many others, firmly established;

798the two dramas Vidagdha- and Lalita-madhava, the bhanika named Dana-keli, and the pair of Rasamritas;

799the Mathura-mahima, the Padyavali, the Nataka-chandrika and the Abridged Sri Bhagavatamrita — these are compilations.

800And among the works of the elder are the precious Srila Bhagavatamrita, the Hari-bhakti-vilasa and its commentary Dik-pradarshini,

801the Lila-stava, and this commentary, the Vaishnava-toshani, which has been abridged by me, the insignificant Jiva, at his command.

802Whatever I have written here hastily, unknowingly or knowingly, and whatever I have left out — may these [elders] forgive me both; and whatever has come forth from me — if that is all my strength, enough of misgivings.65

803This auspicious commentary was completed in [Shaka] 1476, and abridged in 1504."

804So I have named the books of the Gosvamis;
now I shall tell of them in more detail — listen.

805Sri Jiva's disciple Krishnadasa Adhikari
described this in detail in his book.66

806Sanatana Gosvami has four books:
the Bhagavatamrita in two parts with a commentary,

807the Hari-bhakti-vilasa with the commentary Dik-pradarshini,
the commentary on the Tenth Canto called the Vaishnava-toshani,

808and the Lila-stava, which is called the Dashama-charita:
these are the four books of Sanatana Gosvami.

809Thus [it is said]: "The list of compilations of conclusions among the works of the elder of them, named Sri Sanatana, is this:

810first, the Bhagavatamrita in two parts, the Hari-bhakti-vilasa with its commentary Dik-pradarshini, the Lila-stava, and the commentary called the Vaishnava-toshani."

811Sri Rupa Gosvami wrote sixteen books,
revealing the utmost limit of both the pastimes and siddhanta:

812the poems Hamsa-duta and Uddhava-sandesha,
the Krishna-janma-tithi-vidhi with all its injunctions,

813the Ganoddesha-dipika in a larger and a smaller [recension],
the Stava-mala, the Vidagdha-madhava full of rasa,

814the Lalita-madhava — the utmost limit [in depicting] separation,
the Dana-lila-kaumudi — an ocean of bliss,

815known by the name Dana-keli-kaumudi,
the incomparable Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu,

816the book Sri Ujjvala-nilamani, full of rasa,
the sweetest book Prayuktakhyata-chandrika,

817the well-known Mathura-mahima and Padyavali,
the Nataka-chandrika and the Laghu-bhagavatamrita.

818At the Vaishnavas' wish he composed eleven verses
and gave them to Krishnadasa Kaviraja to expand;67

819in them are the pastimes of the eight periods of the day, a supreme elixir;
only the fortunate relish it.

820Briefly he also composed the Viruda-lakshana,
but it is not counted among the books:

821it is the definition [for] his Govinda-virudavali;
the two are one, hence it is known as the "Lakshana".

822Thus [it is said]: "Among the works of the younger of them are the poem Sri Hamsa-duta, the Srimad Uddhava-sandesha, the Injunctions on the Day of Krishna's Birth,

823the Sri Ganoddesha-dipika, known in a larger and a smaller [recension], the beautiful Stava-mala on Sri Krishna and His beloveds,

824the famous Vidagdha-madhava and also the Lalita-madhava, the Dana-lila-kaumudi and also the Bhakti-rasamrita,

825the [Ujjvala-]nilamani, the Prayuktakhyata-chandrika, the Mathura-mahima, the Padyavali, the Nataka-chandrika

826and the Abridged Sri Bhagavatamrita — these are compilations. In the guise of a cowherd boy Gopala Himself, the son of Nanda, appeared to these two in the play of bringing them milk."

827These are the books of the middle Gosvami;
among them I shall tell of the Stava-mala.

828The Gosvami composed his hymns one by one;
in Sri Jiva's collection they received the name Stava-mala.

829Thus [it is said in it]: "The Stava-mala, composed by the illustrious Ishvara Rupa, the author of the Rasamrita, has been collected by Jiva, who lives after him."68

830Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami has three books:
the Stava-mala, which is called the Stavavali,

831and the sweet Dana-charita and Mukta-charita,
on hearing which great sorrows go away.

832Thus [it is said]: "Among the works of the one named Raghunatha, who became the friend of those two, the Stava-mala and the Dana- and Mukta-charita are known."

833Twenty-five books of Jiva are known:
the Hari-namamrita-vyakarana with its divine method,

834the Sutra-malika, the well-composed Dhatu-sangraha,
the truly wondrous Krishnarcha-dipika,

835the Gopala-virudavali, the Rasamrita-shesha,
the Sri Madhava-mahotsava, special in every respect,

836the well-known book Sri Sankalpa-kalpa-vriksha,
the truly wondrous Bhavartha-suchaka-champu,

837the commentaries on the Gopala-tapani, on the Brahma-samhita,
on the Rasamrita and on the Sri Ujjvala,

838a coherent commentary on the Yoga-sara-stava,
an exposition of the Gayatri from the Agni Purana,

839[a description of] the marks on Sri Krishna's feet according to the Padma Purana
and, separately, of the marks on Sri Radhika's hands and feet,

840the Gopala-champu in two parts, the former and the latter —
what wondrous books he wrote, known to the world!

841The seven famous Sandarbhas, after the manner of the Bhagavata:
the Tattva-, Bhagavat-, Paramatma-, Krishna-, Bhakti- and Priti-;

842these six, and the seventh is the Krama-sandarbha;
in them sambandha, abhidheya and prayojana are revealed.

843Thus [it is said]: "Among the works of Sri Jiva, the son of Sriman Vallabha, are named: the grammar called Hari-namamrita,

844its Sutra-malika, the Dhatu-sangraha used in it, the subtle Krishnarcha-dipika, the Gopala-virudavali,

845the Rasamrita-shesha, the Sri Madhava-mahotsava, the Sankalpa-kalpa-vriksha, the champu Bhavartha-suchaka,

846the commentaries on the Gopala-tapani, on Brahma's Samhita, on the Rasamrita, on the Ujjvala and on the Yoga-sara-stava,

847and also an exposition of the Gayatri in the Agni Purana, [a description] of the marks on Sri Krishna's feet named in the Padma,

848and a collection of the marks on the hands and feet of Her who is a special form of Lakshmi — Sri Vrindavaneshvari;

849the two champus, the former and the latter; and the seven famous Sandarbhas on the Srimad Bhagavatam,

850named Tattva-, Bhagavat-, Paramatma-, Krishna-, Bhakti- and Priti-, and the seventh called Krama-;

851in which the noble [authors] have revealed sambandha, abhidheya and prayojana — all three — like an amalaka fruit on the palm," and so on.69

852So I have told of the four Gosvamis;
much in the same way [earlier] devotees too have described them.

853The essence of these books is understood only by one
to whom Sri Bhakti-devi has shown mercy.

854The Vedas and Puranas sing the greatness of bhakti:
by the strength of bhakti nothing is impossible for a devotee.

855The greatness of bhakti is praised by the Vedas and Puranas,
but the greatness of bhakti is known only to the devotees.

856O friends, this one thing I beg:
may I always sing the greatness of bhakti and of the devotees!

857May I never be touched
by the great unbelievers hostile to the devotees and to bhakti.

858Glory to the devotees of Gaura, wish-fulfilling trees!
Be merciful: let my mind abide at the feet of Srinivasa.

859Srinivasa Acharya Thakura is a jewel of virtues;
the earth considers itself blessed by his gift of bhakti.

860In Gauda, Nilachala and Vrindavana Srinivasa
revealed what was in his heart.

861If I am fortunate, this will be told in detail;
for now I shall tell briefly of his birth and the rest.

862On the bank of the celestial river is the village of Chakhandi;
there he was born in the house of the brahmana Chaitanya.

863There too the chudakarana and other rites were performed;
soon he studied grammar and the rest.

864Hearing of the virtues of Sri Chaitanya-chandra, overcome with prema,
he joyfully sets out via Shrikhanda to the Kshetra,

865with the desire in his heart to see in Nilachala
Sri Chaitanya-chandra and His associates.

866While still on the way he heard that Sri Chaitanya had disappeared,
and became such that it seemed life would not stay in his body.

867The Lord, who loves His devotees, the Lord of their lives,
at once appeared to him in the guise of a dream.

868He comforted him, and he, receiving the Lord's command,
came to Nilachala and saw the Lord's dear associates.

869There the Lord's associates showed him great mercy,
and at their command he came to Gauda.

870His heart is constantly in turmoil and nothing can console him;
again he sets out for Nilachala from Shrikhanda.

871Before reaching Jajpur he heard
that Gadadhara Pandita Gosvami had disappeared.

872Unconscious, he falls to the ground and rolls on it,
and weeps so that stones melt to hear it.

873In the guise of a dream Pandita Gosani comforted him,
and from there he went back to Gauda.

874Like a madman he sits down wherever he happens to be
and tells no one anything of the anguish of his heart.

875One day, walking along the road to Gauda,
he heard that Nityananda and Advaita had disappeared.

876What became of him — who can tell?
He firmly resolved to give up his life.

877In the guise of a dream both Lords appeared to him
and comforted him, lovingly speaking sweet words.

878Rising in the morning, he set out for Gauda
and visited Navadvipa and all the other places.

879By way of Shrikhanda he hastened to Vrindavana
and gave himself to the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta.

880There he met Narottama
and studied the books of the Gosvamis.

881To bestow those jewels of books,
he came to Gauda at the command of all the Gosvamis.

882In Vana-Vishnupura the king stole the books —
and, having returned the books, gave himself to his lotus feet.

883Sri Sarakara Thakura arranged his marriage;70
after some time he went again to Vrindavana.

884Again from Vrindavana he came to Gauda,
and his joy with Narottama increased without limit.

885Prabhu Virachandra showed him great mercy,
and day and night he was absorbed in the rasa of sankirtana.

886Everywhere he gave away the jewels of the books of bhakti,
and all the unbelievers and wretches were purified.

887With all the disciples he accepted
he joyfully relished the rasa of bhakti.

888In Gauda he revealed boundless bliss,
and after some time he went again to Vrindavana.

889His journeys to Gauda and to Vrindavana —
by hearing of them desires are fulfilled.

890I have told this briefly; it will be told more fully later;
be merciful, listeners, and accept it.

891I am utterly ignorant and know nothing of the art of poetry;
as best I can, I glorify the lives of the devotees.

892Leaving far behind the thieves who argue,
dive without cease into this Bhakti-ratnakara.

893Meditating on the feet of Srinivasa Acharya,
Narahari Dasa tells the Bhakti-ratnakara.

Thus in the Sri Bhakti-ratnakara ends the first wave, called "A Brief Statement of the Birth of Srinivasa Acharya and Other Events", with the mangalacharana and accounts of various matters.

  2. So in the editions of 1888 and 1912/13 ("shri-bhakti-ratna-pradanaika-daksha", "shachinandana-prema-rupa", "shrinivasa-dvijendra"); the 1960 edition reads differently: "best of devotees, uniquely skilled", "whose form is golden like the son of Shachi's", "Shri-nilaya" (= Srinivasa).
  3. CC Adi 1.1.
  4. Vasu is Vasudeva Ghosha and Madhava is Madhava Ghosha (the kirtan-singer brothers); Shankara is Shankara Pandita, the brother of Damodara Pandita.
  5. The brahmana Haridasa is Haridasa Acharya (Dvija Haridasa), the father of Gokulananda and Shridasa (on them see further in this taranga). "The son of the Acharya" (acharya-nandana) is probably Achyutananda, the son of Advaita Acharya; the reading "the brahmana Haridasa, the son of the Acharya" is also possible.
  6. Shashthidhara ("Yashtidhara" in the 1912/13 edition) is not identified. Vamshi is Vamshivadana; Saranga is Sarangadhara (Saranga Thakura); Sundara is probably Sundarananda.

  8. The division of the Lord's pastimes into an Adi-, a Madhya- and a Shesha- (Antya-) khanda and their contents (43–44) follow the Chaitanya-bhagavata of Vrindavana Dasa.
  9. "Balai loiya mari" — "to die taking another's misfortunes upon oneself": a common Bengali expression of tender love (cf. 65).
  10. A couplet from the Chaitanya-bhagavata of Vrindavana Dasa (the old editions have "tathahi Chaitanya-bhagavate"); the chapter has not been verified.
  11. The source of the verse is not stated. "Brahma-sutra" here may mean both the Vedanta-sutra (the truth it reveals) and the brahmana's sacred thread (upavita) with which the Lord is adorned in Navadvipa.
  12. That is, discrepancies between the accounts of different authors are explained by the pastimes recurring in different kalpas with variations; this is a usual argument of Gaudiya Vaishnava authors (cf. CC, CB).
  13. CC Madhya 9.82–83 (quoted with small variants).
  14. In the CC (Adi 10) Gopala Bhatta is named among the Lord's branches without mention of his father; in Murari Gupta (3.15.15) he is the son of Trimalla Bhatta. Narahari follows the tradition that makes Venkata his father.
  15. The source of the verse is not given ("said by the ancients").
  16. Gopala's vision: the Lord appears to him first as Shyama-Krishna in cowherd dress, then golden (as Gaura) in the same cowherd attire (114–118), and finally in the form of a sannyasi (119).
  17. "Trikachchha" — a dhoti tucked in three places, as cowherds wear it.
  18. "Your disciple" is Srinivasa Acharya, the disciple of Gopala Bhatta who brought the books of the Gosvamis to Gauda (on him see further).
  19. Hari-bhakti-vilasa 1.2.
  20. Gadadhara Pandita served the Deity of Tota-Gopinatha in Puri; "Mishra's house" is the house of Kashi Mishra, where the Lord lived.

  22. An allusion to Srinivasa Acharya, who will bring the books of the Gosvamis to Gauda.
  23. The Lord's cord (dor), kaupina and outer cloth (bahirvas). In the Prema-vilasa (vilasa 1) the Lord sends Gopala Bhatta His waist-cord and seat.

  26. Cf. CB: Vrindavana Dasa repeatedly says that details of the Lord's pastimes "Vedavyasa will describe in the Puranas"; here Narahari calls Vrindavana Dasa himself an incarnation of Vyasa.
  27. On the prohibition by Gopala Bhatta and Lokanatha Gosvami against Krishnadasa Kaviraja writing about them, cf. the Prema-vilasa and the Narottama-vilasa.
  28. Govardhana is apparently the landholder Govardhana Majumdar, the father of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, famed for his generosity. The drama Sangita-madhava is attributed to Govinda Kaviraja (Govindadasa), Ramachandra's brother.

  30. CC Madhya 11.92.
